answer: Verdict: CBA converted best; WBC's conversion was positive but only cushioned a decline; NAB converted worst. The ordering is set almost entirely by the direction of the credit impairment line, because all three banks ran negative jaws (expense growth above income growth). CBA is the only bank where the preferred measure grew faster than the pre-provision line, and both grew: cash-basis operating performance rose 3% to $15,469m and cash NPAT from continuing operations rose 4% to $10,252m, with loan impairment expense down 9% to $726m and the effective tax rate flat at 30.5% - the credit line amplified genuine growth (+0.8pp conversion gap on disclosed dollars). WBC achieved a similar positive conversion (+0.5pp): a 21% fall in impairment charges to $424m (5bps of average gross loans vs 7bps) turned a -3% pre-provision result ($10,548m) into a -2% net profit ex-Notable Items ($6,972m) - but the uplift only cushioned a decline WBC created itself through 9% expense growth (including a $273m Fit for Growth restructuring charge) against 3% income growth. NAB converted worst (-1.5pp): underlying profit rose 1.3% to $10,965m but cash earnings fell 0.2% to $7,091m, because NAB was the only major with rising credit costs - the credit impairment charge rose 14.4% to $833m on $964m of individually assessed charges (business lending and unsecured retail) net of a $131m collective release - plus non-controlling interests doubling to $39m. Comparability limits: the three measures are not the same construct (CBA cash NPAT excludes hedging/IFRS volatility and acquisition/disposal items; NAB cash earnings also excludes amortisation of acquired intangibles and is after NCI; WBC's ex-Notables measure excluded only hedging items in FY25, Large items nil, so it is the least adjusted); each bank keeps different one-off costs inside its 'underlying' result (WBC $273m restructuring, NAB $130m payroll remediation, CBA ~$130m remediation/Bankwest restructuring provisions); CBA's year ends 30 June versus 30 September for NAB and WBC; and NAB/CBA restated FY24 comparatives, so growth sits on each bank's own restated base. Confidence: 82/100.

Net profit excluding Notable Items is a non-AAS financial performance measure used by Westpac for management reporting as it better reflects the underlying performance of the Group.

limitations: The three preferred measures exclude different items and no document reconciles one bank's basis to another's; the conversion comparison is therefore directional, not like-for-like.
CBA's year ends 30 June 2025 while NAB's and WBC's end 30 September 2025, so the three results cover different rate and credit windows.
Disclosed percentage movements are rounded; the conversion gaps (+0.8pp CBA, +0.5pp WBC, -1.5pp NAB) are computed from the disclosed $m figures, not printed.

Pre-provision lines are each stated on the bank's own adjusted basis (CBA cash, NAB cash earnings, WBC ex-Notable Items) and keep different one-off costs inside, so 'pre-provision performance' is not a single common construct.
NAB and CBA restated FY24 comparatives; growth rates sit on each bank's own restated base.

The disclosures do not attribute NAB's tax and non-controlling-interest movements to specific drivers, and do not quantify how much of each bank's impairment movement reflects overlay or collective-provision judgment versus loss experience.
